title: If a function is awaited and later the owning object is freed, the call just hangs
body:
### Tested versions

4.7.stable

### System information

Arch Zen Linux latest - Godot v4.7.stable

### Issue description

When awaiting a coroutine from another function and queue_free is used on the owning object, the await just hangs forever. This wasn't the case in 4.6.stable. It seems if the object is freed in 4.7, any couritines running under it is canceled, but that doesn't release the awaiting callers this can produce a very confusing and unexpected hang in await calls which would be hard to debug.

Ideally, the engine releases the await in case the coroutine was canceled due to owning object being freed.

### Steps to reproduce

For some npcs, I have a goto function, and a gate object that deletes the npc, when it gets to the gate to simulate the npc going through the gate.

```
class_name npc
func go_to(target: Node2D):
    while not is_queued_for_deletion():
        if target_reached(target): break
        await get_tree().process_frame
        # go to logic
```

Then I have an event that controls this npc and starts the next event, something like

```
class_name event
@export
var character: npc
@export
var target: Node2D
@export
var next: event
func do_event():
    await character.go_to(target)
    next.do_event()
```

The gate does

```
_on_body_enter(body: Node2D):
    if body is not npc:
        # do something else
        return
    npc.queue_free()
```

Now when the npc gets to the gate, I'd think it ends the coroutine, but instead the coroutine hangs, hanging the entire event chain.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mrp-coroutine-hanging.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29692935/mrp-coroutine-hanging.zip)
